question: A 28-year-old man with a 4-year history of inflammatory back pain has restricted lumbar flexion (Schober's test 2 cm), sacroiliac joint tenderness, and a lateral spine X-ray showing flowing calcification of the anterior longitudinal ligament with fusion of vertebral bodies. HLA-B27 is positive. Which radiological finding BEST explains this appearance, and what is its pathological basis?

answers.text: Romanus lesion — erosions at the discovertebral junction causing the 'shiny corner' sign on MRI.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Romanus lesions (shiny corners) are the earliest radiological finding in AS and represent inflammatory enthesitis at the anterior vertebral corners, but they describe focal erosions on MRI — not the late confluent fusion described here.

answers.text: Bamboo spine — ossification of the annulus fibrosus forming syndesmophytes that bridge vertebral bodies, producing a continuous column.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The 'bamboo spine' is the pathognomonic late radiological sign of AS. It results from progressive ossification of the outer annulus fibrosus (enthesitis at disc–vertebral junctions) forming vertically oriented syndesmophytes that eventually bridge adjacent vertebral bodies, creating the characteristic continuous column appearance. This is distinct from the non-marginal osteophytes of DISH.

answers.text: Pencil-in-cup deformity — resorption of the terminal phalanx with surrounding periosteal new bone at the DIP joint.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The pencil-in-cup deformity is the pathognomonic radiological sign of psoriatic arthritis (PsA), not AS. It reflects severe erosive arthritis at DIP joints where the bony ends taper into a cup-like concavity. In AS, the spine and sacroiliac joints are primarily affected.

answers.text: Juxta-articular osteopenia — periarticular bone loss from synovial hyperaemia, seen at sacroiliac joints.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Juxta-articular osteopenia is an early non-specific radiological feature seen in RA and other inflammatory conditions. It does not explain the flowing calcification and vertebral bridging described in this case.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review AS radiology: bamboo spine results from syndesmophyte formation (enthesitis → annulus ossification → vertebral bridging). Pencil-in-cup is PsA (DIP); Romanus lesions are early AS on MRI, not late fusion.

Well done. Bamboo spine = late AS hallmark, caused by syndesmophyte bridging from annulus fibrosus ossification. Contrast with pencil-in-cup (PsA, DIP joints) and juxta-articular osteopenia (RA, early).
